newsitem.title: FRANCE: Brunei agency buys Paris's luxury Meurice Hotel.
newsitem.headline: Brunei agency buys Paris's luxury Meurice Hotel.

text.p: The Audley Group, a prestige hotel company owned by the Brunei Investment Agency, announced on Friday that it had bought the luxury Meurice Hotel in Paris from the Aga Khan's Abbots Fields SA.
The 200-year-old Meurice, which overlooks the Tuileries Gardens in the heart of the French capital, has 152 rooms and 28 suites as well as a one-star restaurant.
It served as German headquarters in Paris during World War Two, and Salvador Dali and the Duke and Duchess of Windsorhave been among its guests.
No price was given for the transaction.

The Audley Group, which owns the prestige Dorchester Hotel in London and the Beverly Hills Hotel in Los Angeles, said in a statement that it would "preserve the Meurice's personality, which has made it one of the most reputable hotels in the world".
The Brunei Investment Agency is controlled by the Sultan of Brunei Sir Hassanal Bolkiah. Its investment portfolio is estimated at $40 billion to $60 billion.
The Aga Khan is the wealthy spiritual leader of the Shia Ismaili Moslems.
